input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility fixes for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic delivers keyboard operability for the four audited core Dashboard
flows — project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run
submission — by fixing every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit
report: focus lost in modals, controls unreachable by keyboard, and
inconsistent focus indicators. The Dashboard is the single-pane web console
for the platform; after this epic, a user can complete each of the four flows
end-to-end with keyboard input alone.

## Scope

- Remediate the audit-enumerated keyboard defects in the project creation
  flow, workbench spawn flow, model deployment flow, and pipeline run
  submission flow of the Dashboard.
- Focus management in modals and dialogs used by the four flows: focus moves
  into the dialog on open, cycles within it, and returns to the triggering
  control on close (no focus traps).
- Keyboard reachability and operability of every interactive control in the
  four flows (tab order, arrow-key navigation where applicable, Enter/Space
  activation, Escape to dismiss).
- Consistent, visible focus indicators on all focusable controls across the
  four audited flows.
- Out of scope (per strategy): screen-reader semantics beyond what the
  keyboard fixes require, and any flows outside the four audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the project creation flow, when it is operated with keyboard input
  only, then it can be completed end-to-end without pointer input; measured by
  a keyboard-only walkthrough that dispositions every audit defect recorded
  for that flow.
- Given the workbench spawn flow, when operated with keyboard input only,
  then it can be completed end-to-end without pointer input; measured by the
  same per-flow keyboard-only walkthrough.
- Given the model deployment flow, when operated with keyboard input only,
  then it can be completed end-to-end without pointer input; measured by the
  same per-flow keyboard-only walkthrough.
- Given the pipeline run submission flow, when operated with keyboard input
  only, then it can be completed end-to-end without pointer input; measured by
  the same per-flow keyboard-only walkthrough.
- Given any modal or dialog in the four flows, when it opens, then focus
  moves into it and cannot escape the dialog while it is open; when it closes,
  focus returns to the control that triggered it; measured by a per-dialog
  focus-trap check covering every modal in the audited flows.
- Given any interactive control in the four flows, when the user tabs or
  arrow-navigates to it, then it is reachable and operable via keyboard and
  presents a visible, stylistically consistent focus indicator; measured by a
  control-by-control keyboard pass over the four flows.
- Given the Dashboard test suite, when the accessibility fixes are applied,
  then the existing automated tests still pass; measured by the suite run on
  the merged changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): the four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls — covered by the per-flow
  keyboard-only walkthrough, focus-trap, and reachability acceptance criteria
  above.
- HLR-2 (P1): visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows — covered by the focus-indicator consistency acceptance criterion
  above; delivered in the same epic as HLR-1 because both requirements touch
  the same controls, modals, and flows in one remediation pass.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
— the VPAT (conformance statement) and the product documentation's
accessibility statement — so that it accurately reflects the fixed,
keyboard-accessible state of the four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission). Two
public-sector customers require the updated, published conformance statement
before renewal, making the published documentation a first-class deliverable
of the strategy alongside the code fixes.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT so its conformance claims for keyboard operability reflect
  the implemented fixed state of the four audited Dashboard flows.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to describe the
  current accessibility posture of those flows.
- Republish both artifacts through the Red Hat documentation content process
  so the updated conformance statement is publicly available.
- Technical review of the updated content against the implemented Dashboard
  behavior before publication.
- Out of scope (per strategy): conformance claims for screen-reader semantics
  beyond what the keyboard fixes require, and for flows outside the four
  audited ones.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the implemented keyboard-accessibility fixes for the four audited
  flows, when the VPAT is updated, then every keyboard-operability conformance
  claim in it matches the shipped behavior of those flows; measured by a
  claim-by-claim comparison of the updated VPAT against the implemented
  state.
- Given the product documentation, when the accessibility statement is
  updated, then it accurately describes the keyboard-accessible state of the
  four audited flows; measured by the same claim-by-claim comparison.
- Given the updated VPAT and accessibility statement, when they undergo
  technical review, then a technical reviewer confirms in writing that the
  documented claims match the implemented behavior; measured by a completed
  review sign-off recorded before publication.
- Given the reviewed content, when it is republished, then the updated VPAT
  and accessibility statement are available at their published product
  documentation location; measured by retrieving the published artifacts and
  confirming they contain the updated conformance claims.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P2): the accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product
  docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the
  fixed state, with technical review — covered in full by the acceptance
  criteria above.

authoring — the VPAT and accessibility statement rewrite and republication

code change; it is a separately-published deliverable that two public-sector
customers require for renewal, produced through the Red Hat docs content
